bc_hig_s_zone.blurb: Hig's Zone is a small crag inside Higgyland, a sport-climbing area on the hillside above the waterfront near Powell River, now called qathet. It holds nine routes, eight bolted and one trad, with grades from 5.8 up into the 5.11 range, spread fairly evenly between 5.10 and 5.11. The formation offers a low-angle wall with a gully running along its right side, plus a steeper vertical face around on its south side. To find it, follow the trail that starts on the left of the neighbouring Destruction Zone.

bc_right_2.blurb: Right is the first sector you meet on the approach trail at The Beach, a roadside crag on Highway 1 east of Savona, near Kamloops. Its nine sport routes cover a wide spread, from the easiest grades up to a single 5.11, with most clustered around 5.10. The sector comes into view as the path swings back toward the cliff, which makes it an easy place to begin a visit. Across The Beach, routes are bolted with chain anchors and run roughly 7 to 20 m, with good views from the base.

bc_chuck_chuck_creek.blurb: Chuck Chuck Creek is a remote group of sport crags up a logging road in the Squamish Valley, north of Squamish. Its nine routes run from 5.10 to 5.12, mostly 5.10 and 5.11, and the climbing across the wider group is largely single-pitch. The rock dries quickly after light showers, though a long wet spell can leave seeps on some lines. There is no phone coverage at the crags, so plan a self-sufficient day. The logging road is rough at the start, so allow extra driving time.

bc_colossus.blurb: Colossus is a sunny sport crag in the Squamish Valley, close to the High Falls Creek trail. It has two walls: a main face up to 60 m with routes of up to three pitches, and a smaller wall of single-pitch lines up to 35 m. The nine routes here are mostly 5.11 and 5.12, with one easier line near 5.8 and one 5.10. Winter sun makes it a good cool-weather choice, while summer afternoons turn hot. A 70 m rope is recommended, and phone signal in the valley is poor to nonexistent.
bc_colossus.parking_note: Small pullout on the right side of Squamish Valley Road, roughly 400 m past the hydro station and bridge and before the High Falls Creek trailhead. It fits only two or three cars.
bc_colossus.approach: Walk back about 10 m along the road you drove in on to find the trail, then follow it steeply uphill to the base, about 15 minutes.

bc_the_ledge.blurb: The Ledge is a compact bolted crag on a narrow shelf of rock in the Squamish Valley, reached from the Ashlu forest road. Its nine sport routes run 17 to 29 m, steep with crack features, with grades from low 5.10 up to 5.13, mostly 5.11 and 5.12. Fixed lines help you move along the ledge between routes. The wall faces northwest and stays shaded until about 3 pm, and in autumn it is in shade all day. Spring seepage is common, but the lines tend to dry fast and then stay dry. A 60 m rope reaches the ground from most routes, though a couple are close.
bc_the_ledge.parking_note: Pullout directly opposite the 4 km sign on the Ashlu forest road, which branches left over a bridge off Squamish Valley Road. The road is steep and rough but does not need four-wheel drive.
bc_the_ledge.approach: The crag is visible from the pullout. Take the short trail up and to the left until you arrive at the ledge.
